title: Javascript ES6 Import, Export and Modules Practice
summary: Practice with named exports and imports: export four calculator functions from calculator.js and import them into the React app so a four-item list shows computed results. Solved both with named imports and with a wildcard import.

concepts.heading: Exporting several functions
points: calculator.js has add, multiply, subtract and divide and no default export, so they are exported as a named group: export { add, multiply, subtract, divide };.
Export the function itself, with no parentheses; adding parentheses would call it rather than export it.
Until the import is in place, the app reports errors such as 'add is not defined'.

concepts.heading: Importing them
points: Named import: import { add, subtract, multiply, divide } from "./calculator"; The order inside the braces does not matter, only the exact names.
The source is a relative path to the file; the .js extension may be omitted.
Wildcard alternative: import * as Calculator from "./calculator"; then call Calculator.add(1, 2) etc. The namespace object holds one property per export.
Both approaches work and both appear in real code, so recognise each.

task.name: Import the calculator functions
task.starting_point: A sandbox whose App renders four list items calling add, multiply, subtract and divide, plus calculator.js defining them without exporting, and a Final.png of the target.
task.goal: Make the page render four calculated numbers by exporting and importing the functions.
steps: Open calculator.js and export all four functions as named exports.
In the file that renders the list, import add, multiply, subtract and divide with braces from the relative path of calculator.
Remove the 'not defined' errors and compare with Final.png.
Optionally redo it with import * as Calculator and prefix each call.
task.expected_result: Four bullet points showing 3, 6, 5 and 2.5 (results of add(1,2), multiply(2,3), subtract(7,2), divide(5,2)).

solution_code.code: import { add, multiply, subtract, divide } from "./calculator";

task.reference_repo_path: Section 36 - React.js/36.15 Javascript ES6 Import, Export and Modules Practice/es6-import-export-practice

pitfalls: Exporting with parentheses (add()) calls the function instead of exporting it.
Names in the import braces must match the export names exactly.
With the wildcard form every call needs the namespace prefix.

gaps_and_ideas: Use as the practice task in an 'ES6 modules' lesson: export and import four helper functions, then redo with a wildcard.
Interactive demo: a small calculator module whose exports can be toggled on and off to show which imports break.
